statement: You are given a string s of uppercase English letters and an integer k.
You may change at most k characters of s, each into any uppercase letter. Return the length of the longest substring that can be made to consist of a single repeated letter.

A window can be made uniform when its length minus the count of its most frequent letter is at most k. Slide a window over s, shrinking it from the left whenever it needs more than k changes, and keep the longest valid length.

examples.explanation: The window "BABB" (indices 2 to 5) has three B's and one A. Changing that A gives "BBBB", length 4. No window of length 5 has only one letter out of place.
With no changes allowed, the answer is the longest existing run of one letter: "BBB" or "AAA", both of length 3.

constraints: s consists of only uppercase English letters
